correctness.rationale: Direct add/subtract identities of the cyclic equations partition every distinct real pair into antipodal and asymmetric cases. The resulting sum/product equations admit exactly 0, 1 or 3 unordered real primitive 2-cycles with sharp steps 2 and 3. Inverse branch calculus yields the products (2h-5)^2 and 9-2(h-1)^2; their zeros and unit crossings provide exact singular, repelling, neutral and attracting intervals. The fixed-point derivatives then prove the sharp six-attractor threshold. A second algebraic check factors H_h(H_h(x))-x into fixed-point, antipodal and quartic asymmetric factors. The embedded verify.py completed 106 exact symbolic assertions across rational steps and algebraic boundary values; finite tests do not replace the proof. Singular transitions are explicitly excluded from smooth-Floquet claims.

originality.rationale: The Nov 9 2026 motivating paper treats the same cubic backward-Euler component and provides the antipodal orbit and its multiplier, but its full Section 7 does not classify asymmetric pairs or identify the sharp h=1+sqrt(5) all-six-attractor threshold. The Nov 2 2026 initiating paper treats general local cyclic Lyapunov-Schmidt reductions rather than the explicit all-parameter census. The published same-cubic published-finding corpus repeller theorem proves a 3-symbol full shift only for h>=64, which implies large-h existence of three two-cycles but not sharp birth, singularity or all-sink thresholds. The older theta-method papers discuss spurious 2-cycles generally, not this explicit full census. Historical priority remains a documented risk.
residual_risks: An earlier general theorem or historical textbook may specialize to the same all-h sharp cubic census; absence from search results is not a proof of priority.
The 1991 Iserles–Peplow–Stuart paper was compared through its abstract and available scholarly text, not an independently page-complete inspection; a hidden equivalent example is possible.
The 2019 Green–Patrick–Spiteri paper was inspected only through publisher abstract and figures; uninspected body remains a lesser-priority risk.
The same-cubic 2026 repeller theorem already implies the large-h existence portion, so no novelty is asserted for that subclaim in isolation.

value.rationale: The exact finite-step threshold at which a double-well implicit discretization admits six locally attracting periodic orbits (three constant and three period-two), even though the scalar ODE has no nonconstant periodic orbit, quantifies a substantial solver-branch dynamical artifact. The 0/1/3 primitive-cycle classification and distinct fold versus flip thresholds explain its mechanism and give a natural complete all-step invariant. This is not a narrow arbitrary parameter slice; it is the full scalar cubic normal-form family for the step-size variable, and the sharp thresholds occur before the previously established large-step full-shift regime.
